title: fix(rest)!: POST /batch answers an update or delete op whose id names no row with the missing-id 400, not a 500
body:
Fixes #24781

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changed

`POST /api/v1/batch` (the cross-object transactional batch, and its environment-scoped twin from the same registrar) checked up front that an `update` / `delete` op names a row. But it tested only for an absent or `null` id: `op.id == null && op.data?.id == null`. An id the engine does not take as one passed that check and reached `ql.update` / `ql.delete`. The engine's `Update requires an ID or options.multi=true` / `Delete requires an ID or options.multi=true` throw then answered as a server fault.

The fix is in `packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts`:

- `batchOpRowAddress(op, data)` is the one reading of the row an op addresses. `update` reads `id`, else `data.id` (the arm's own `op.id ?? data?.id`). `delete` reads `id` alone, which is all its arm ever sent. The up-front check and both write arms read it, so the check can no longer pass an op that its arm then sends with no address.
- `namesNoRow(action, address)` judges that address with the engine's own by-id predicates, `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` / `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`. These are the functions `ObjectQL.update` / `ObjectQL.delete` dispatch on, and `@objectstack/rest` already depends on that package. A by-id address is a truthy string or number.
- `isBatchRef` is now the one spelling of the `{ $ref }` test, shared with the ref resolver. An update whose `data.id` references an earlier create is not judged up front; the resolver still refuses an unresolvable one with `BATCH_UNRESOLVED_REF`.

The refusal's code and sentence are the ones a missing id already got: `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `Operation 'update' on 'OBJECT' requires an id` (or `'delete'`).

## Contract

These are all the inputs whose answer changes. Before, the transaction opened, the engine threw and the batch rolled back, so nothing was written. Now the batch is refused before the transaction opens, and nothing is written.

| op on cross-object `POST /batch` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `update`, `"id": ""` (the card) | `500 DATABASE_ERROR`, "Internal data error" | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `Operation 'update' on 'OBJECT' requires an id` |
| `update`, no `id`, `data.id` is `""`, `0`, `false`, `true`, `{}` or `[]` | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` | the same `400` |
| `update`, `"id": ""` beside a real `data.id` (`id` is read first) | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` | the same `400` |
| `delete`, `"id": ""` (the card), with or without a `data.id` | `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, "Internal server error" | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `Operation 'delete' on 'OBJECT' requires an id` |
| `delete`, no `id`, the record's id only in `data.id` | `400 INVALID_FILTER`, the engine's filter guard ("Filter comparand at where.id is undefined …") | the same `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` "… requires an id" |
| any of the above, where a later step used to answer first (the per-object API-exposure gate's `404` / `405`, or another op in the batch) | that later step's answer | this `400`. The id check runs before the exposure check and the transaction, as it already did for a missing id |

These answers do not move, and the pins below hold them as controls:

- A missing or `null` id gets the same `400`.
- An update by `id` or by `data.id`, and a delete by `id`, write as before.
- An update whose `data.id` is `{ "$ref": 0 }` still resolves to the row created by op 0.
- An unknown id answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. So does a whitespace id (`"  "`), which the engine looks up like any other id.
- `atomic: false` still answers `400 BATCH_NOT_ATOMIC` first, because that check comes before this one. With `atomic: true` and with `atomic` omitted, the rule is the same.

The delete-by-`data.id` row is fixed in place under the bounded exemption. It is the same defect class (the up-front check passed an op that its arm sent with no address), in the same check, the same file and the same gate family. Leaving it out would mean the check knowingly accepts `data.id` for a delete while the arm ignores it.

## Which ids count as missing

The rule is "refuse what can never address a record", judged by the engine. Measured with `resolveEngine*Dispatch` and with the `500`s above on `main`:

- `""`, `0`, booleans, objects and arrays are never a by-id address, so they are refused.
- A whitespace string is a by-id address. The engine and the driver look it up, and the answer is an honest `404`, so it is not refused here.
- `null` in `data.id` was already refused.
- `op.id` is `z.string().optional()` in the spec, so a non-string `id` is still refused by the schema (`Invalid batch request`) before this step.

This is not id-format validation.

## Other doors that serve the operation

- The per-object `POST /data/:object/batch`, `updateMany` and `deleteMany` have no REST-level up-front id check. The protocol's row check is `if (!record.id) throw rowRequiredIdError(…)`, a falsy test. Measured with the same real-engine harness:
  - `update` / `delete` rows with `"id": ""` answer a per-row `VALIDATION_FAILED`, "Record id is required for update" (or delete).
  - `deleteMany` with `ids: [""]` answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`.
  - A whitespace id answers a per-row `404`.
  
  These doors do not share the gap, so there is no shared helper.
- `@objectstack/runtime`'s dispatcher has no `/batch` branch. `domains/data.ts` routes only `query`, and `http-dispatcher.ts` reports `transactionalBatch: false` for exactly that reason. There is no twin.

## Tests

The new `packages/rest/src/rest-batch-blank-id.test.ts` runs a real engine (`ObjectQL` + sqlite `SqlDriver`), the real protocol and the real route, with `objectQLProvider` wired. It has:

- 11 refusal rows. Each asserts the whole `{ status, body }` (status, `code` and sentence), that `engine.transaction` was never called, and that the seeded row is unchanged.
- One row proving that an earlier `create` in the same batch is not written.
- 8 controls, the ones listed above.

Red and green:

- On `main` `a43405d59`, the pin file gave **12 failed / 8 passed**. Update rows answered `500 DATABASE_ERROR`, delete `""` rows `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and delete-by-`data.id` `400 INVALID_FILTER`.
- Ablation 1, with the fix committed: `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` swapped the check back to `op.id == null && op.data?.id == null`. The landing was proven by the anchor count going 1 → 0 and the blob going `c2ad0e6dac7e` → `7be150e2b515`. Result: **12 failed / 8 passed**, the same rows.
- Ablation 2: the `isBatchRef` carve-out deleted. Exactly the `$ref` control failed (`expected 400 to be 200`).
- Both ablations were restored with blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- After the fix: pin file 20/20. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` on `0d4ea3e5b` (after merging `origin/main` `307ce4c4b`): **305 files passed, 6144 tests passed, 326 skipped**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` (tsc plus the test-layer check) exited 0.

## Gates (local, on `0d4ea3e5b`)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 67 commands for this diff against merge base `307ce4c4b`. All 67 ran and exited 0, with each exit code captured before any pipe. The `--ran` reconciliation reports 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`), the family the derivation does not name: exit 0.
- `test:repo` (the `repo` vitest project) was not run locally. The diff touches none of its five files, and CI's `Test Core` runs it.

## Changeset

`@objectstack/rest`: **minor**, carrying this PR's narrowing declaration line and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition. The dispatch asked for `patch`. Measured on a throwaway commit object (no branch or tree change): `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` with this PR's declaration line and a `patch` grade on `@objectstack/rest` exits 1 ("clause-② declares `no (narrowing)` while no moved package is graded `minor` or above"). With `minor` it passes. A narrowing ships `minor` in the launch window.

## Acceptance notes

- The engine's `Update requires an ID…` / `Delete requires…` throws still answer `500` wherever another caller reaches them, with `DATABASE_ERROR` and `INTERNAL_ERROR` disagreeing between the two verbs. That mapping is held off here: it is the door-parity region of #24768, which carries it.
- The spec's `CrossObjectBatchOperationSchema.id` is `z.string().optional()` with no `.min(1)`, so `""` passes the schema and reaches this check. Tightening the schema would move the refusal to `Invalid batch request` with a different sentence. That is `packages/spec`, held off, and not a defect after this fix. Noted, not filed; no carrier.
